newsitem.title: USA: Universal Seismic holders seek to block board vote.
newsitem.headline: Universal Seismic holders seek to block board vote.

text.p: Universal Seismic Associates Inc was sued Monday by two shareholders seeking to delay for 30 days the election of directors scheduled for the annual meeting on January 28.

In papers filed in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Michael Kanarellis of Houston and Robert Kecseg of Dallas, Texas, owners of 5.0 percent of Universal's shares, alleged that proxies sent to shareholders in advance of the meeting were "materially false and misleading."

On December 6 the plaintiffs began a competing proxy consent solicitation for their own slate of directors. They claim Universal has incurred net losses in three of the last four years and that as of September 30, its total debt equalled 97 percent of stockholders equity.

According to Kanarellis and Kecseg, merger negotiations with Suelopetrol c.a. were terminated last fall when the Venezuela-based seismic contractor rejected demands by Universal management seeking "to entrench itself" with salary increases and five year contracts.
Kanarellis is the president and principal stockholder of TechnoFlex Inc, a marketing company which initiated the merger talks, court papers said.

Universal Seismic is a Houston-based oil and gas exploration business that provides seismic contracting services and performs global position surveys (GPS) used by the seismic industry. Its energy arm is UNEXCO Inc.
A hearing on the lawsuit is scheduled on Wednesday before U.S. District Court Judge Roderick McKelvie according to a court spokwoman.
Mawelek, the chairman of Universal Seismic, was unavailable for comment.
